Definition: properly, plowing, i.e. (concretely) freshly plowed land
BiblicalUsage: Freshly plowed land is the picture of a heart ready for seed. Proverbs says much food is in the tillage of the poor, and the plowing of the wicked is sin; Jeremiah and Hosea both cry, break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns, for it is time to seek the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fallow ground is my heart: it must be broken up before it can be sown, and the plowing is the work of repentance. The tillage of the poor feeds many, and the plowing of the wicked is sin — the same ground, two opposite harvests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
